Presenting Complaints:

- Daily diarrhea since surgery

- Request for Ativan for travel anxiety

- SI joint pain bilateral - pain in back, shoulder area

- Pain unchanged despite physiotherapy

- Attended physiotherapy 7 times - feels better on 2016-12-03 of treatment

- Performing home exercises as instructed

- Groin pain mostly resolved, lingering slightly

- Able to walk

- Diarrhea twice daily - first bowel movement pure water, second soft/mushy

- No solid bowel movements since surgery

- Eating well




Self-Treatment:

- Stopped gabapentin 300mg bid 2012-12-29 - did not like how it made her feel

- Zofran PRN for nausea - stomach much better

- Not taking anything for diarrhea - prefers to let it clear system




Impact:

- Three surgeries in 1992-12-16 - does not want another surgery

- Upcoming travel - 1989-03-26 drive up north in 1983-01-26, flying 2012-01-10




Past Medical History:

- History of Crohn's disease with IBS-D

- History of small bowel infection

- Entyvio infusions 2005-10-29 without complications

- Diabetes - managed by dr. Patient 1473 with insulin

- Previous steroid injections - first worked well for 2012-08-08, second did not work and caused blood sugar issues requiring hospitalization




Objective:

- Post-op report from Patient 2595 dated 1998-02-06: 1980-06-13 with history of back pain presenting for post-operative follow-up for decompressive surgery/discectomy. Overall definitive improvement in symptoms. Wound very well healed. Persistent rt anterior thigh and groin pain with muscle cramping - nerves recovering. SI joint pain bilateral secondary to altered weight bearing following lumbar surgery. Recommended physiotherapy to improve strength and function. Advised continued avoidance of strenuous activities including gardening. Instructed to monitor for worsening pain. Continue use of walker for balance issues. Conservative treatments prescribed. SI joint injection may be considered if pain persists.




Assessment & Plan:




1. Post-operative lumbar stenosis surgery - SI joint pain bilateral

- Diagnosis: SI joint pain secondary to altered weight bearing following lumbar surgery

- Treatment planned: Continue physiotherapy. Lyrica prescribed - 30 pills, start at nighttime due to drowsiness. May consider SI joint injection (lidocaine without steroid) if pain persists.




2. IBS-D

- Diagnosis: IBS-D - gastroenteritis

- Treatment planned: Probiotics (Align) recommended. Follow-up with dr. Patient 1472 in 1994-04-01.




3. Diabetes

- Diagnosis: Diabetes

- Treatment planned: Continue management with dr. Patient 1473 for insulin.




4. Travel anxiety

- Treatment planned: Ativan prescribed for upcoming travel.

Subjective:




Chief Complaint:

- Back pain radiating down rt leg for over a week

- Believes this is sciatica




Onset and Duration:

- Over 1971-06-18

- No identifiable trigger - no lifting, no physical activity, no yard work




Location and Quality:

- Pain starts in lower back, radiates down rt leg to foot

- Shooting, constant pain




Aggravating and Alleviating Factors:

- Sitting worsens pain significantly

- Prolonged sitting in car particularly bothersome

- Home exercises (leg raises) - not effective

- Heat and cold application - not effective

- AquaFit in pool - took it easy, uncertain if helpful




Associated Symptoms:

- No numbness or tingling

- No bowel or bladder incontinence

- Saddle sensation intact

- No fever




Impact on Function:

- Mobility affected - walking slowly

- Walks with a limp




Past Medical History:

- Spinal stenosis

- Bilateral hip replacements

- History of breast cancer x2 - 2017-08-23, cancer-free since

- History of myocardial infarction

- Ozempic for weight loss - lost 22 lbs

- Constipation - on stool softener

- Variable blood pressure - previously noted to be low by Dr. biswa

- Current medications: Tylenol arthritis 2 tabs bid, Ozempic, stool softener

- Has Ramacet remaining from 1980-11-20 (prescribed for different issue)

- Baclofen prescribed but not taking since 2024-12-14




Objective:




General:

- Gait: limping, slow




Back Examination:

- Erythema over lower back from heating pad use

- Tenderness on palpation of lower back

- Pain radiates down rt leg on examination

- No tenderness on upper back palpation




Neurological:

- No numbness or tingling

- Bowel and bladder control intact

- Saddle sensation intact




Assessment & Plan:




1. Sciatica - rt leg

- Diagnosis: Sciatica

- Treatment planned: Continue Tylenol arthritis 2 tabs bid; may take additional dose between doses if needed; continue heating pads

- Referrals: Physiotherapy referral for 1975-07-20 - has coverage, attends Patient 2243 in Tecumseh

- Investigations planned: If symptoms persist after 2013-05-14 or worsen, or if bowel/bladder symptoms or numbness/tingling develop - X-ray and CT scan of back and/or bone scan to be arranged

- Rtc if pain does not subside in 1988-06-25 or if red flag symptoms develop

- Follow-up with Dr. biswa end of July

Subjective:

- Presenting Complaint: Suture removal following left index finger injury

- Mechanism of Injury: Cut finger while trimming hedges in yard 1974-11-27; was holding a branch when cut occurred

- Initial Management: Bleeding difficult to control; called 911, then 811, advised to see doctor by 2015-04-26; daughter transported to emergency; seen by Dr. Patient 90; received 5 local anaesthetic injections; 5 sutures placed; tetanus vaccination administered; splint applied; discharged at 2016-03-03 with antibiotic prescription

- Post-Procedure Course: Throbbing for 1991-05-21 after freezing wore off; took Tylenol after discharge; completed antibiotic course (last dose 2022-09-13)

- Current Symptoms: Pain with finger movement; whole hand soreness; difficulty with 1998-08-21 activities including eating and making sandwiches




Past Medical History:

- History of trigger finger repair 2005-04-02

- Lives alone; daughter is caregiver




Objective:

- Wound Inspection: 5 sutures in situ (3 vertical, 2 horizontal); wound healing well; nail split but flat, not lifted

- Sensation: Intact to light touch and movement
